plan_default: 200 trials per model (Heretic default) = 131 min GPU per model = 262 min for two models
decision: The full 2 x 200-trial budget does NOT fit alongside the four-checkpoint evaluation. Per fallback F3 the optimizer budget is REDUCED SYMMETRICALLY instead of asymmetrically: both models get 60 TPE startup trials + the same number of TPE trials in the resume, chosen from the clock after both phase-A runs finish. Equal budget in both models is the property the core comparison depends on, so an unequal 200-vs-60 split is rejected even though it would use more GPU time.
consequence: Selections are made from a matched but SMALLER-than-default budget and are labelled accordingly; each journal stays resumable to 200 via `uv run method.py --stages phaseB_<tag>`.

final_matched_budget.composition: 60 TPE startup trials (identical draws in both models) + 56 TPE trials
final_matched_budget.how_it_was_enforced: Heretic restores the phase-A settings on resume, so the stored n_additional_trials=140 overrode the CLI value and the GaMS resume headed for 200 trials. GaMS was stopped with SIGINT after 116 complete trials (Heretic's objective_wrapper turns KeyboardInterrupt into study.stop() plus one PRUNED trial - trial 116 - which is recorded and excluded from every analysis). The driver then gained --stop-at-trials, and Gemma was run to exactly the same 116 complete trials, so the two optimizer budgets are equal by construction.
final_matched_budget.deviation_from_plan: 200 trials per model was the plan; 116 per model is what the wall clock allowed alongside the four-checkpoint evaluation. The reduction is SYMMETRIC - an unequal budget would have broken the matched design that the whole comparison rests on. Both journals remain resumable to 200.
